images.title: The Bill of Rights, as proposed by Congress in 1789
images.caption: The Bill of Rights dated 25 September 1789: the enrolled original of the joint resolution in which the Congress 'begun and held at the City of New-York' proposed twelve articles of amendment to the United States Constitution. Articles three to twelve, ratified in 1791, became the first ten amendments; article two became the Twenty-seventh Amendment in 1992, and article one was never ratified. On this document the First Amendment is 'Article the third', so today's Fourth Amendment appears as 'Article the sixth'.

Checked OK, upstream: hai.stanford.edu/news/ai-index-state-ai-13-charts exists ('AI Index: State of AI in 13 Charts', Shana Lynch, April 15, 2024) and embeds the same chart (AIIndex_2024_StateofAI_BLOG_13.jpg). 'When asked in a survey about whether AI products and services make you nervous, 69% of Aussies and 65% of Brits said yes.' returns FOUND. Stanford campus coordinates (37.4275, -122.1697) are right.

Independent check of the numbers: AI Index 2024 Chapter 9 (Figure 'Opinions about AI by country (% agreeing with statement), 2023', Source: Ipsos, 2023) and Ipsos 'Global Views on A.I. 2023' (July 2023), p.10, both give Australia 69%, Great Britain 65%, Canada 63%, United States 63%, India 58%, France 52%, Spain 51%, Belgium 50%, Germany 46%, South Korea 44%. Every figure in the caption and alt text is correct.

Precision problem 1, population and wording: the survey statement was 'Products and services using artificial intelligence make me nervous' (% agree very or somewhat). Ipsos asked 22,816 adults under 75 in 31 countries between May 26 and June 9, 2023. The survey was online-only except in India, and the India sample is 'more urban, more educated, and/or more affluent than the general population'. The caption says 'people ... who say AI makes them nervous', which repeats the chart's shorthand title rather than the question actually asked.

Precision problem 2, selection: the chart shows 10 of the 31 countries surveyed. It leaves out New Zealand (63%, tied with Canada and the US) and Ireland (62%), both of which rank above India. The caption's 'in each country' could be read as covering every country, and HAI's own alt text ('Australia ..., Great Britain ..., and Canada at 63% top the list') can make the chart look like a complete ranking. The corrected caption states that the chart is a selection, so the page does not present it as 'the most nervous countries'. Japan was lowest at 23% and is not shown.

Minor: 'Stanford HAI licensed the chart ... by email permission' is basically right. More exactly, the uploader got permission by email from the AI Index research manager, and Wikimedia's Volunteer Response Team archived it under ticket #2024060510011799, approving publication under CC BY-SA 4.0. The corrected caption uses that wording.
